raw: | CodeQL `go/unsafe-unzip-symlink` on a tar extractor that already checks the joined path and the symlink target — looks like a false positive | It is not. A **chain of two symlinks** escapes: the guard resolves each link against its **lexical** parent while the OS resolves it against its **real** one. `sub/up -> ..` genuinely is the root (allowed, correctly); `sub/up/w -> ..` therefore really is `root/w`, pointing at the root's **parent**, and lexically looks like `root/sub`. Then `sub/up/w/pwned` contains no `..` and passes every check | `cmd/mxcli/docker/download.go` — one `extractTarGzInto` on `*os.Root` behind both `extractTarGz` and `extractTarGzStrip1`, plus `tarEntryPath` / `symlinkStaysInside` / `pathWithin` | **Try to break it before rating it, and keep trying after the first six attempts fail.** Six single-step archives (absolute link, `../..` link, absolute name, link-to-root, …) were all correctly refused, which is exactly what makes "false positive" tempting; the seventh — two chained up-links — wrote a file into the extraction root's parent, and an eighth reached any sibling directory. The fix is `os.OpenRoot` + `Root.OpenFile`/`MkdirAll`/`Symlink` (Go 1.24/1.25), which hands containment to the kernel (`openat2` `RESOLVE_BENEATH`) instead of to string comparison — the failure is then `path escapes from parent` from the OS. Keep a **link-target** check as well and resolve its parent with `EvalSymlinks`: `os.Root` stops *mxcli* following an outward link, not mxbuild or the JVM that read the tree afterwards. Two things the rewrite fixed for free: `strings.Contains(name, "..")` silently dropped legitimate files (`foo..bar` never appeared, no error) — `filepath.IsLocal` is the right test, on path *elements* — and a `HasPrefix` containment test with no separator puts `/cache/runtime-evil` inside `/cache/runtime`. Settle "would refusing break real downloads?" by measurement, not caution: the 11.13.0 CDN tarballs are 3,646+279 (runtime) and 33,188+5,036 (mxbuild) entries with **zero symlinks**, listed with `curl \| tar -tzv` without saving the archive. Control both directions — the ordinary-archive test must pass, and against the old extractor the chained cases must actually write outside (they do, in both the stripping and non-stripping variants). |
